A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViewFusion with the same authors, core architecture, and NMR benchmark. Text, equations, tables, figures, and all appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original NMR evaluation scores in Table 2 and generated examples demonstrating weighting, occlusion handling, autoregressive generation, and variable view counts.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds a quantitative view-count analysis and experiments on relative poses, unseen classes, and weighting ablations.

M1.justification: The main U-Net, learned weighting, loss, and sampling algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix D.1 adds a trained variant conditioning the target angle relative to the first input view instead of the dataset-defined canonical pose. This is a limited adaptation of the conditioning procedure.

E1.justification: NMR remains the sole evaluated dataset. Appendix D adds focused scenarios involving a first-input-relative target pose and generalization to cars excluded from training. The latter tests an unseen category rather than merely unseen instances. Objaverse, CO3D, and MVImageNet are proposed future datasets, not evaluated additions.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains LFN, PixelNeRF, SRT, and ViT for NeRF with unchanged scores. Appendix D.3 introduces simple averaging as an internal comparator, both trained from scratch and substituted into an already trained weighted model. Newly cited external methods are not added to the evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocol and main training settings are retained, but the evaluation design expands substantially. New protocols include testing 1, 2, 3, 6, and 9 input views on a test subset, canonical-versus-relative validation comparisons, retraining with cars excluded, and separate training-time and inference-time averaging controls. These are additional experiments, not revisions of Table 2's settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative sensitivity to input count in Figure 2, a canonical-pose assumption test in D.1, an unseen-category robustness example in D.2, and two complementary weighting ablations in D.3. These substantially extend the original qualitative demonstrations and directly test the central aggregation mechanism.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 retains three single-view evaluations, the same reported standard deviations, and one multiview evaluation. The added analyses introduce no stated repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original qualitative results are unchanged. New results include improving scores with input count, weighted-versus-averaged training curves, and unseen-car generation collapsing beyond approximately 180 degrees. D.1 reports canonical versus relative validation PSNR of 31.17 versus 26.54 and SSIM of 0.95 versus 0.89. D.3 reports inference-time averaging reducing validation PSNR from 27.38 to 25.88 and SSIM from 0.90 to 0.88. These are newly reported comparisons under additional settings.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects the expression introduced as the score: v1 repeats the probability-mixture expression, whereas v2 displays the gradient of the log probability. The subsequent derivation, mixture assumptions, and diffusion mathematics otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its performance comparison from state-of-the-art methods to comparable methods, and the introduction replaces the state-of-the-art contribution claim with competitive performance. The central claims about composable diffusion, flexible pose-free inputs, and generative handling of occlusion remain.

C2.justification: D.1 explains the coupling between object semantics and dataset-defined canonical poses and attributes relative-pose degradation to task difficulty. D.3 explains why individual streams can remain useful under averaging. Section 5 qualifies 3D-asset applications as requiring a separate image-to-3D approach and realistic dataset augmentation as requiring successful scaling.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies uniform input-count sampling and random view selection without proximity bias. Appendix B.1 adds approximately two-minute inference, batching behavior, and capacity of 28 samples with six conditioning views on one 32GB V100. Existing training hyperparameters, aggregation pseudocode, and code access are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against newer work, including LEAP, RenderDiffusion, MultiDiff, SyncDreamer, Zero123++, Cascade-Zero123, and MVDiffusion++. It distinguishes pose requirements, fixed input grids, and inability to extrapolate input counts, refining the flexibility argument beyond v1's narrower comparison. Additional dataset references support future directions.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory explanation, edits wording throughout, updates author and publication information, and reverses the acknowledgments/impact-statement order. Appendix D is added, but the main section sequence and most existing methodological and theoretical prose remain closely matched.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout, extensively relocating and resizing figures, tables, and algorithms. Four new figures present the added analyses. Existing qualitative figures are retained and renumbered, while Figure 1 receives corrected timestep and output labels.

improvement.justification: v1 supported its central learned-weighting contribution mainly through benchmark scores and qualitative visualizations. v2 adds retrained and inference-time averaging controls that directly establish its empirical benefit, addressing an important validation gap. Relative-pose and held-out-category experiments also expose applicability limits, while performance claims become more restrained. These substantially strengthen the paper's evidential basis, although the new analyses leave subset sizes and uncertainty insufficiently documented.
